verdict.rationale: ROS 2 ships its own SROS2/DDS-Security tooling. With it you create a keystore and security enclaves, each of which encapsulates a single policy and can be mapped to processes, users, or devices. That works as scoped, per-participant credentials that could be issued to an agent node. The evidence does not show these as API credentials built for agents, nor does it detail granular least-privilege permissions. Missing for 10: explicit per-topic/service least-privilege permission scoping in evidence, agent-oriented credential issuance/rotation/revocation workflow, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: A security enclave encapsulates a single policy for protecting ROS communications.
Security enclaves can be flexibly mapped to processes, users, or devices at deployment.
Use the sros2 utilities to create the keystore. Files in the keystore will be used to enable security for all the participants in the ROS 2 graph.
enables authentication of participants sending data
